claim_types.source-observed: Behavior directly established by pinned code and an executable invariant; no product outcome is claimed.
claim_types.source-inferred: A user-visible prediction derived from a pinned source path and paired with a falsifier; not a measured result.
claim_types.runtime-observed: A product outcome established by a reproducible runtime trace.

Cost.claim: The direct DeepSeek fetch/SSE adapter on the shipped agent path predicts lower provider-seam latency and exposes cache-token amplification.
Cost.falsifier: A same-model trace shows extra blocking calls or no meaningful latency, token or request advantage.

Compatibility.claim: Native DeepSeek translation plus the agent-operable Cordis seam predict less semantic loss and a shorter extension path.
Compatibility.falsifier: Same-model substitution loses no useful semantics, or a representative extension still needs core edits, restart or manual cleanup.

Continuity.claim: Write-behind coordination on the default JSONL persistence path predicts resumability without putting every storage operation on the response hot path.
Continuity.falsifier: Persistence blocks useful output, loses required events on recovery, or creates unacceptable crash-loss tails.

Cost.claim: A dependency-ranked repository map with an explicit token budget predicts lower context and orchestration tax on repository edits.
Cost.falsifier: Representative cross-file tasks need more repair turns or tokens because decisive context is omitted.

Compatibility.claim: Model configuration and command surfaces expose provider and model differences on the shipped CLI path.
Compatibility.falsifier: The required model or edit-format differences still require application-side adapters.

Continuity.claim: Git commits, guarded undo and lint/test feedback predict a short and reversible correction loop.
Continuity.falsifier: Git mediation loses user edits or costs more correction time than it saves.

Cost.claim: The DOM serializer emits a compact interactive representation instead of raw page HTML.
Cost.falsifier: Serialization consumes as many tokens or as much time as the generic browser representation it replaces.

Compatibility.claim: DOM-to-model serialization predicts fewer grounding failures than a generic screen or raw-HTML path.
Compatibility.falsifier: Matched tasks show no reduction in stale, ambiguous or ungrounded browser actions.

Continuity.claim: A persistent browser session with reconnect/watchdog behavior and serializable agent state predicts fewer lost-session failures.
Continuity.falsifier: Recovery loses browser or agent state, or watchdog/reconnect work worsens success and tail latency.

Cost.claim: Parallel-safe tool calls can overlap while preserving model-visible result order.
Cost.falsifier: Representative tasks contain no safe overlap or scheduling adds more delay than it removes.

Compatibility.claim: First-class MCP session and exposure machinery predict lower tool-integration friction on governed repository work.
Compatibility.falsifier: Required tools still need bespoke mediation or MCP lifecycle overhead dominates the task.

Continuity.claim: Rollout reconstruction and session state predict lower recovery loss across long coding work.
Continuity.falsifier: Resume loses decisive state or reconstruction costs more than rerunning the bounded task.

Cost.claim: Routing and compression are shipped policy paths with executable tests.
Cost.falsifier: Routing and compression add context churn or latency without lowering task cost.

Compatibility.claim: Live extension loading and policy-aware integration predict safer customization with fewer restarts.
Compatibility.falsifier: Representative extensions still need restart/manual repair or can bypass required policy.

Continuity.claim: Checkpoint utilities and an integration-tested recovery path predict lower edit loss after interruption.
Continuity.falsifier: Checkpoint recovery loses user edits or adds more repair work than it prevents.

Cost.claim: The launcher exposes explicit local/cloud provisioning paths, but no default-path yield edge is established.
Cost.falsifier: Provisioning and frontend/server hops dominate useful work.

Compatibility.claim: One launch service selects and mediates local and cloud conversation backends.
Compatibility.falsifier: Backend differences leak into manual operator repair or prevent comparable task execution.

Continuity.claim: Claim-before-network launch, lineage and workspace isolation predict fewer duplicate launches and cross-agent conflicts.
Continuity.falsifier: Lineage cannot reconstruct outcomes or shared-workspace fallback causes unacceptable conflicts.

Cost.claim: The layered runtime exposes orchestration control but no isolated low-amplification edge for the named terrain.
Cost.falsifier: Runtime layers add more calls, tokens or repair work than they remove.

Compatibility.claim: A shared session client and structured events predict lower friction when moving among IDE, CLI, SDK and remote clients.
Compatibility.falsifier: Cross-surface transport creates stale UI, duplicate state or manual migration.

Continuity.claim: Checkpoint restore and a stateful orchestration runtime predict reversible sessions across interruption and client changes.
Continuity.falsifier: Restore loses user edits or the live session diverges across clients.

Continuity.claim: Pending writes and checkpoint conformance predict less repeated work after a peer node fails.
Continuity.falsifier: Resume repeats completed effects or checkpoint overhead dominates the representative workflow.

Cost.claim: Pre-call budget, cache-affinity and routing policy predict more verified outcomes per constrained dollar or quota.
Cost.falsifier: Routing raises total cost or TTFT without improving externally verified completion.

Compatibility.claim: Exception-specific retry/fallback and provider translation predict fewer quota and availability failures across providers.
Compatibility.falsifier: Fallback loses decisive provider semantics or hides task failure behind a successful response.

Compatibility.claim: The bundle contract and graph runtime provide shipped extension and composition mechanisms.
Compatibility.falsifier: A representative component still requires core edits or bespoke deployment glue.

Continuity.claim: Checkpoint construction, storage and resume paths exist with an executable durable-store test.
Continuity.falsifier: Resume repeats effects, loses graph state or remains unavailable on the default deployment path.

Compatibility.claim: The A2A wrapper and integration tests establish a reachable remote-agent mediation path.
Compatibility.falsifier: Role or remote-agent differences still require custom orchestration and duplicated context.

Continuity.claim: Flow persistence and resumability are implemented and exercised, without yet establishing a net yield edge.
Continuity.falsifier: Resume loses flow state or role handoffs amplify calls and failure edges beyond recovered work.

Cognition.claim: Unified memory is reachable, but automatic policy improvement and rollout/rollback are not established.
Cognition.falsifier: Stored memory does not affect later execution, or it changes behavior without attributable policy control.

Cost.claim: Bounded workflow dispatch can overlap independent work without exceeding the configured concurrency limit.
Cost.falsifier: Representative tasks expose no safe overlap, or orchestration overhead dominates.

Compatibility.claim: Runtime refresh updates MCP, LSP, skills, subagents, hooks and memory without requiring a process restart.
Compatibility.falsifier: Extension changes still require restart or partial refresh leaves inconsistent runtime state.

Continuity.claim: Recovery classifies interrupted histories and repairs orphaned tool calls before continuation.
Continuity.falsifier: Interrupted sessions lose decisive state or resume duplicated unsafe effects.

Cost.claim: Token-budgeted compaction and protected recent turns predict lower context tax without orphaning tool output.
Cost.falsifier: Compaction omits decisive context and creates more repair work than it saves.

Compatibility.claim: Provider adapters preserve tested provider-specific reasoning fields, aliases and model semantics.
Compatibility.falsifier: A required provider semantic is dropped or requires application-side translation.

Continuity.claim: Snapshot-backed reverse patches and message cleanup predict reversible session recovery.
Continuity.falsifier: Revert loses user work, leaves later state attached, or cannot reconstruct the prior state.

Cost.claim: Provider-aware cache breakpoints preserve exact reusable prefixes and predict lower repeated-context cost.
Cost.falsifier: Matched traces show no cache reuse or cache mediation increases total cost.

Compatibility.claim: The shipped extension manager exposes native MCP transports and tool capabilities on the agent path.
Compatibility.falsifier: Representative extensions require core edits or lose required tool semantics.

Continuity.claim: SQLite session storage and prefix-preserving fork behavior predict durable, non-destructive continuation.
Continuity.falsifier: Fork or resume mutates the source session, drops messages, or repeats effects.

Cost.claim: Automatic threshold compaction and bounded tool output are shipped on the LLM runner path.
Cost.falsifier: Compaction calls or missing context cost more than the context they save.

Compatibility.claim: Provider plugins preserve tested provider-specific options and custom provider identities.
Compatibility.falsifier: Required provider controls are normalized away or need core changes.

Continuity.claim: Ordered projection and staged revert state predict reconstructable, reversible sessions.
Continuity.falsifier: Projection reorders events or committed reverts cannot restore coherent state.

Cost.claim: Budget-aware message compilation preserves system, tools and recent tool sequences while pruning older context.
Cost.falsifier: Pruning drops decisive context or increases repair turns and total tokens.

Compatibility.claim: Tested stdio, SSE, HTTP and WebSocket MCP transports predict broad extension compatibility.
Compatibility.falsifier: A representative MCP server needs bespoke mediation or loses required semantics.

Continuity.claim: Session history save, load, list and delete behavior is implemented and executable-tested.
Continuity.falsifier: Interrupted writes corrupt history or resume omits decisive session state.

Cost.claim: Token-estimated automatic compaction preserves recent context and file operations under tested budgets.
Cost.falsifier: Compaction loses decisive state or its extra request increases total time and token cost.

Compatibility.claim: Cross-provider handoff tests preserve reasoning, tool identifiers and message transformations.
Compatibility.falsifier: Provider switching drops reasoning or tool semantics in representative sessions.

Continuity.claim: Atomic repair and fork writes plus torn-tail recovery predict robust JSONL session continuity.
Continuity.falsifier: A crash loses committed events, corrupts the source session, or makes resume unsafe.

Cost.claim: The agent executes multiple same-turn tool calls concurrently and has bounded summarization paths.
Cost.falsifier: Tasks contain no safe overlap or coordination and summarization cost more than they save.

Compatibility.claim: Single-flight MCP renewal and hot configuration reconciliation preserve a shared healthy tool session.
Compatibility.falsifier: Concurrent refresh duplicates sessions or config changes require restart/manual repair.

Continuity.claim: Database-backed sessions persist messages, usage and mutable session state on the workspace path.
Continuity.falsifier: Resume loses required messages or persisted state diverges from the visible session.

Cost.claim: Automatic token-threshold compaction is tested across disabled, small-context and output-limit cases.
Cost.falsifier: Compaction overhead or omitted context increases end-to-end task cost.

Compatibility.claim: Live context-server tool registration and collision disambiguation predict low-friction MCP extension.
Compatibility.falsifier: Tool changes remain stale or collisions expose the wrong tool to the model.

Continuity.claim: Database flush and reopen tests restore messages, drafts, token usage and scroll state.
Continuity.falsifier: Application interruption loses committed thread state or reopen reconstructs an incoherent session.

Cost.claim: Configurable history processors bound observations and cache-control placement on the live message path.
Cost.falsifier: The processors are unused for the target run or removed context increases repair cost.

Compatibility.claim: LiteLLM-backed model configuration exposes fallbacks, message conversion and per-model limits.
Compatibility.falsifier: A required provider semantic is lost or the target model needs bespoke mediation.

Continuity.claim: Per-step trajectories support replay, but source evidence does not establish safe interrupted-session resume.
Continuity.falsifier: Replay duplicates side effects or cannot restore in-progress state.
